_meta.title: AWS Cloud Practitioner Basics
_meta.description: Starter pool with introductory AWS services, pricing, security, and cloud concepts aligned to Cloud Practitioner fundamentals.

questions.text: Which AWS service provides virtual machines in the cloud?
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 provides resizable compute instances.

questions.text: Which AWS service is primarily used for object storage?
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 stores objects such as files, backups, and static assets.

questions.text: Which AWS service offers a managed relational database?
questions.explanation: Amazon RDS manages relational database engines like MySQL and PostgreSQL.

questions.text: Which AWS service is used to manage users, groups, and permissions?
questions.explanation: Identity and Access Management controls access to AWS resources.

questions.text: What is an Availability Zone?

answers.text: An isolated data center location within an AWS Region

questions.explanation: Regions contain multiple Availability Zones for resilience.

questions.text: In the shared responsibility model, what is AWS responsible for?

answers.text: All operating system patching in every case

questions.explanation: AWS secures the infrastructure that runs cloud services.

questions.text: What does Auto Scaling do?

answers.text: Adjusts compute capacity automatically based on demand

questions.explanation: Auto Scaling increases or decreases resources to match workload needs.

questions.text: What is the purpose of Elastic Load Balancing?

answers.text: Distribute incoming traffic across multiple targets

questions.explanation: Elastic Load Balancing improves availability by spreading traffic.

questions.text: Which AWS service is a content delivery network?
questions.explanation: CloudFront caches content close to users for faster delivery.

questions.text: Which AWS service runs code without provisioning or managing servers?
questions.explanation: Lambda is a serverless compute service.

questions.text: What is an Amazon VPC?

answers.text: A logically isolated virtual network in AWS

questions.explanation: A Virtual Private Cloud lets customers define their own network topology in AWS.

questions.text: Which AWS service provides DNS and domain routing features?
questions.explanation: Route 53 provides DNS, health checks, and domain registration features.

questions.text: Which AWS service is used for monitoring metrics and setting alarms?
questions.explanation: CloudWatch tracks metrics, logs, and alarms for AWS resources.

questions.text: Which storage class is intended for data accessed less frequently but requiring rapid retrieval?
questions.explanation: S3 Standard-IA is designed for infrequent access with low latency retrieval.

questions.text: Which AWS service helps manage multiple AWS accounts centrally?
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations supports centralized governance across accounts.

questions.text: What type of storage does Amazon EBS provide?

answers.text: Shared file storage for on-premises printers

questions.explanation: Elastic Block Store volumes attach to EC2 instances as block devices.

questions.text: Which AWS database service is a managed NoSQL key-value and document store?
questions.explanation: DynamoDB is AWS managed NoSQL service for high-scale workloads.

questions.text: What does AWS Trusted Advisor provide?

answers.text: Recommendations for cost, security, performance, and fault tolerance

questions.explanation: Trusted Advisor reviews AWS environments and suggests improvements.

questions.text: Which pricing concept means customers pay only for the resources they use?
questions.explanation: AWS pricing is based heavily on consumption rather than large upfront capital expense.

questions.text: Which AWS tool helps estimate the monthly cost of a planned deployment?
questions.explanation: The AWS Pricing Calculator is used to model expected service costs.
